# Loop structures in widget proteins

Alice Alpha, Bob Beta ^alp20-p001

## Abstract

> [!claim|margin llm supports] Supports
> - [[Short widget loops adopt a small number of canonical shapes]]

<mark class="pm-claim">Most short widget loops fall into five recurring shapes.</mark> We surveyed 400 crystal structures solved by <abbr title="X-ray crystallography">XRC</abbr>. ^alp20-shapes

## 2.1 Results

> [!context|margin llm] Scope
> The survey covers [[Canonical loop|canonical loops]] from crystal structures only.

> [!claim|margin llm supports] Supports
> - [[Widget loops are rigid]]
>
> Rigidity is inferred from low B-factors, not measured directly.

> [!cite|margin llm]- References (2)
> - [[#^alp20-ref-1|1]] Delta D, Alpha A. An early census of widget loops. Widget Letters. 2019. → [[delta2019|Delta (2019)]]
> - [[#^alp20-ref-2|2]] Omega O. Loops in gadgets. Gadget Journal. 2015.

The shapes were assigned for <mark class="pm-context">loops from crystal structures</mark>, extending earlier counts [[#^alp20-ref-1|1]], [[#^alp20-ref-2|2]]. <mark class="pm-claim">Loop backbones showed uniformly low B-factors.</mark> ^alp20-p003

> [!eq|margin llm] Symbols
> $k$ is the number of shapes and $n$ the loop length.

$$
k = \log_2 n \tag{1}
$$
